title: The Anteiglesia and the Flag: Bizkaitarra, Larrinaga, and the Invention of a Nation
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Abando, the house on Ibáñez de Bilbao
stops.date_confidence: attested; the Spanish, English and Basque Wikipedia articles all give 26 January 1865. One strand of the research pool carried 25 January from an institutional biography; no source fetched supports it, and the contradiction is recorded rather than adjudicated. The baptism at San Vicente Mártir is attested only to the year and is narrated at the birth date for ordering. Coordinates corrected to the OpenStreetMap geocode of Ibañez de Bilbao 16.
stops.campa: Santiago Arana Ansostegi, shipbuilder and Carlist, keeps a house built eight years earlier in Abando, an anteiglesia that is not yet Bilbao and is already being eaten by it. Here the eighth and youngest child is born to him and to Josefa Pascuala Goiri, and carried a few doors along to the parish of San Vicente Mártir to be christened Sabino Policarpo. He is born inside the thing he will spend his life refusing. Across the water the foundries are burning for an ore trade that is turning the province into an industrial coast, and the men who work it are arriving from Castile.
suggested_refs: The present Sabin Etxea at Ibáñez de Bilbao 16, standing on the site of the 1857 house
The parish of San Vicente Mártir, Abando, forty metres from the birth address

stops.name: Hendaye, the family crosses the Bidasoa
stops.date_confidence: year only, and contradicted inside the research pool: the chronology dates the exile to 1872, following Santiago Arana's implication in the Carlist conspiracy, while the geography dates the crossing to 1873. Neither is resolved here. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 01. Coordinates corrected to Hendaye's own geocode, about a kilometre east of the value first carried.
stops.campa: The father has run money and supplies for Don Carlos, and when the conspiracy breaks the family goes over the river into France. Hendaye is the ordinary crossing: a Basque town on the far bank where the language does not change and the state does. Sabino is eight, and the first thing a border teaches him is that it saves them. The Aranas will move along that coast for three years, Bayonne, Saint-Jean-de-Luz, Guéthary, staying wherever a Carlist household can be sheltered, and speaking Euskera in every one of those houses.
suggested_refs: The Bidasoa crossing at Hendaye, used by the family in exile and by Arana again in 1902
sources: research pool, geography lens on the 1873-1876 exile itinerary

stops.name: Bayonne, the Collège Saint-Louis-de-Gonzague
stops.date_confidence: attested by es.wikipedia for 1873, with the geography lens giving 1873-1874; month and day unknown, defaulted to 01. Sources disagree on the sequence and continuity of the French schooling, some stressing private tutoring over ordinary classrooms, and that disagreement is left standing.
stops.campa: At the Jesuit college in Bayonne he does his lessons in French, among the sons of a French Basque bourgeoisie for whom Euskera is a kitchen language and the Republic is the state. From eight to eleven, the son of a Biscayan house is educated abroad, in the language of another country. How much of that happened in classrooms and how much with private tutors is disputed; one account has an Álava officer of the Carlist army teaching a boy in exile the war he had just lost. Which arrangement took up most of the three years, no source settles.
suggested_refs: The Collège Saint-Louis-de-Gonzague, Bayonne
Saint-Jean-de-Luz and Guéthary, the other named stations of the exile

stops.name: Hondarribia, the examination on the way home
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the entrance examination at Hondarribia appears in the pool's chronology alone and was not independently confirmed. The Third Carlist War ended in February 1876 and the family's return is attested for that year; month and day unknown, defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: The war ends in February and the frontier reverses its meaning: France stops being refuge and Spain stops being danger. On the way back the boy sits an entrance examination at Hondarribia, on the Spanish bank of the Bidasoa, and passes it. The paper clears him for the Jesuit boarding school at Orduña, inland and high, where Luis will board with him. The family that left in a hurry comes back in an orderly way, by examination and enrolment. He is eleven.
suggested_refs: The Bidasoa frontier at Hondarribia, crossed on the return of 1876

segments.name: Orduña, and the Garden at Abando

stops.name: Orduña, the Colegio de Nuestra Señora de la Antigua
stops.date_confidence: attested for the span 1876 to 1881 by es.wikipedia and eu.wikipedia; the month of entry is not given and is defaulted to 01. Coordinates corrected to the OpenStreetMap geocode of the college on Foru enparantza, about a kilometre from the value first carried in the pool.
stops.campa: Five years boarding with the Jesuits, in a walled town at the bottom of a limestone bowl where the road from Castile climbs into Biscay. Luis boards with him, and here the brothers form the habit of arguing everything out between the two of them. He is taught in Spanish and prays in Latin, and is drilled in a piety he never afterwards puts down: the nationalism he invents later is Catholic before it is anything else, and the banner he carries into Navarre at twenty-nine will put God ahead of the old law.
suggested_refs: The Colegio de Nuestra Señora de la Antigua, Orduña, Jesuit boarding school of both Arana brothers

stops.name: Orduña, the bachillerato taken from the bed
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 1881 by es.wikipedia; the day is not given and is defaulted to 01. That he sat the final examinations while bedridden is reported by es.wikipedia and repeated widely. The separate prolonged convalescence at sixteen that later accounts describe is supported only obliquely and is a reconstruction.
stops.campa: He takes the final examinations of the bachillerato lying down, with a lung disease his biographers call tuberculosis, and passes them with strong marks. Illness is the constant from here to the end: the pulmonary years, then the digestive ones, then the adrenal collapse at thirty-eight. He goes home to Abando to recover, into a house where politics is the daily talk and the sons have nothing to do but read. What he read that summer is not recorded.
suggested_refs: The examination record of the Orduña bachillerato, June 1881

stops.name: Abando, the garden and the conversation with Luis
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to date and setting. Easter Sunday 1882 did fall on 9 April, and eu.wikipedia places the conversation on Easter Sunday, but no source fetched attests the garden. The pool reports that the historian José Luis de la Granja argues the precise Easter dating and the resurrection symbolism were systematised only in 1932, for the first Aberri Eguna; that argument could not be confirmed from a fetched source and is carried as an unverified lead.
stops.campa: Luis, three years older, has already worked it out and spends the afternoon saying so: Carlism is a Spanish dynastic cause, and a Spanish cause cannot restore Biscay, because Biscay is not a region of Spain but a nation of its own. Sabino argues, and loses, and by evening he holds the position he will spend twenty-one years elaborating. The whole later movement dates itself from this hour, Easter Sunday, resurrection and all, and marks the wall of the house with a plaque fifty years afterward. What the brothers actually said to each other nobody wrote down that day.
suggested_refs: The plaque placed on Sabin Etxea in 1932 marking the 1882 conversation
José Luis de la Granja Sainz on the 1932 systematisation of the Easter dating
sources: sabinoarana.eus, efeméride on the conversation of 9 April 1882

stops.name: Abando, the death of Santiago Arana
stops.date_confidence: year only; es.wikipedia gives 1883 for the death of Santiago Arana Ansótegui without a month, defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: The father dies. Santiago Arana had built ships and moved supplies for the Carlist army, and with him gone the widow Pascuala decides the family will go to Barcelona, where the sons can be got degrees. Sabino is eighteen and a year into his conversion, and he wants neither law nor Barcelona. It is the last time in his life that he lives anywhere by somebody else's decision. He goes because his mother asks him to, and the first article and the first book of his life are both written there.
suggested_refs: The Arana family house at Abando, later Sabin Etxea, built by Santiago Arana in 1857

segments.name: Barcelona and the First Printed Word

stops.name: Barcelona, enrolled in law and letters
stops.date_confidence: attested for the span 1883 to 1888 by es.wikipedia and eu.wikipedia; the month of enrolment is not given and is defaulted to 01. Coordinates corrected: the pool carried 43.3729, -2.1637, which falls in the Bay of Biscay some five hundred kilometres from Barcelona, with the latitude replaced and the longitude sign flipped. The value used is the historic building of the Universitat de Barcelona at Plaça Universitat.
stops.campa: He matriculates in Law and in Philosophy and Letters and attends when it suits him, which is seldom. What he reads instead is philology, natural history, and the historians of the Basque provinces; what he watches is a Catalan revival already twenty years into the work of making a language respectable and a nation arguable. He takes the lesson and rejects the model, and will write a pamphlet against Catalanism for founding a nation on language rather than descent. Five years in the city, and no degree at the end of them.
suggested_refs: Errores catalanistas (1894), Arana's pamphlet against the Catalan model of nationality

stops.name: Bilbao, the first printed word
stops.date_confidence: attested to 15 July 1886 by es.wikipedia. The office address of the Revista de Vizcaya was not located; the pin marks the old-town publishing district at city-block precision.
stops.campa: The question in the title is whether the word should be written with a b or a v, and the answer runs to a claim about who the Basques are and where their name comes from. It is a piece of orthography that behaves like a manifesto. Arana is twenty-one and publishing into Bilbao from five hundred kilometres away. The article also opens the quarrel with Miguel de Unamuno, Bilbao-born and philologically trained, who will spend decades insisting the Basque language is dying and ought to be allowed to die in peace.
suggested_refs: '¿Basco o Vasco?', Revista de Vizcaya, 15 July 1886, Arana's first printed article
sources: bvfe.es, author record for Sabino Arana

stops.name: Barcelona, the Pliegos histórico-políticos
stops.date_confidence: attested to 7 April 1888 by es.wikipedia. The quotation is transcribed as Granja prints it, against a lightly modernised version carried in the pool.
stops.campa: His first book, printed in the city he dislikes, and already carrying the position that will make him impossible to absorb: autonomy is not a stage on the road to independence but a substitute for it, and a fatal one. Regional self-government, he argues, would be accepted, administered, and then forgotten, and the nation would die of the concession. He is twenty-three. Fourteen years later, from a cell in Larrinaga, he will publish an article proposing the most radical autonomy possible within the unity of the Spanish state.
stops.quote: ¡ay de Euskeria el día que abrazara la autonomía: ese día atraería sobre su cabeza la sentencia de muerte!
stops.quote_source: Pliegos histórico-políticos, Barcelona, 1888, in Obras Completas (1965), pp. 75-76, as quoted by José Luis de la Granja Sainz, 'La concepción de la autonomía en el pensamiento político del Nacionalismo Vasco: I. La Restauración'
suggested_refs: Pliegos histórico-políticos, Barcelona, 1888
Granja, 'La concepción de la autonomía en el pensamiento político del Nacionalismo Vasco: I. La Restauración'

stops.name: Bilbao, the chair of Vascuence and Resurrección María de Azkue
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1888 by es.wikipedia, which gives the vote as eleven for Azkue, three for Unamuno and none for Arana; month and day are not given and are defaulted to 01. The pool first carried this as an unconfirmed episode of the 1890s and the correction is recorded.
stops.campa: The Instituto de Bilbao creates a chair of Basque and three men stand for it: Resurrección María de Azkue, priest and lexicographer, who will spend his life on the dictionary and the academy; Unamuno, who thinks the language is finished; and Arana. Azkue takes eleven votes, Unamuno three, Arana none. The man who is about to invent a spelling system, a vocabulary, a calendar of new given names and a name for the country itself receives not one vote to teach the language. Azkue takes the chair and keeps it. Five years later Arana starts his own newspaper instead.
suggested_refs: The 1888 competition for the chair of Vascuence at the Instituto de Bilbao

stops.name: Barcelona, the death of Pascuala Goiri
stops.date_confidence: year only; es.wikipedia gives 1888 for the death of his mother in Barcelona without a month, defaulted to 01. It falls in the same year as the failed competition at Bilbao and the publication of the Pliegos, and the pool does not order the three events against each other.
stops.campa: Pascuala Goiri dies in Barcelona, and the reason for staying dies with her. Sabino abandons both faculties without taking anything from either and goes north with his sister Paulina. He leaves with no degree and no employment, and with a complete theory of a nation that does not yet know it is one. Behind him are five years of lecture halls he barely entered and one printed book. Four more years pass before he publishes again, and what he publishes then is a book of old Biscayan battles.
suggested_refs: The 1888 return of Sabino and Paulina Arana from Barcelona to Biscay

stops.name: Begoña, the oath at the Larrazabal farmhouse
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the exact day: eu.wikipedia carries 3 June 1893 for the Larrazabal dinner, while es.wikipedia dates the speech to 1893 without a day. The pin approximates the Begoña hillside where the farmhouse stood; the plot itself is not confirmed.
stops.campa: The year before, he had published four narratives of legendary Biscayan battles under the title Bizkaya por su independencia, on the argument that the resistance had never once stopped. Now seventeen men of the Euskalerria circle give him a dinner in a farmhouse above Bilbao, and he stands up after it and tells them where he came from: a Carlist boyhood, a brother's argument on an Easter afternoon, a conversion. Then, in front of all of them, he swears to work until his death for the independence of Biscay.
suggested_refs: The Discurso or Juramento de Larrazabal, 1893
Bizkaya por su independencia. Cuatro glorias patrias (Bilbao, 1892)

stops.name: Bilbao, the first number of Bizkaitarra
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 1893 by es.wikipedia; the day, 8 June, comes from the Sabino Arana Fundazioa's note on the printer Sebastián de Amorrortu and was not independently confirmed. Amorrortu's street address is not given by the source and the pin approximates the old-town printing district.
stops.campa: Printed at Amorrortu's shop in the old town, owned by him, directed by him, written almost entirely by him: thirty-two numbers over two years, attacking liberals, Spanish nationalism, and the Castilian and Galician workers pouring into the ore basin. The prose is deliberately unbearable and is prosecuted repeatedly. It is also the first time the argument exists as an object a man can carry across a province in his coat. Twenty-six months after the first number the club is sealed, the paper is suppressed, and he is inside Larrinaga.
stops.quote: El nacionalismo bizkaino tiende a la constitución de Bizkaya en nación absolutamente libre e independiente de las demás.
stops.quote_source: Bizkaitarra (Bilbao, 1893-1895), as quoted in José Luis de la Granja Sainz, 'La concepción de la autonomía en el pensamiento político del Nacionalismo Vasco: I. La Restauración'
suggested_refs: The thirty-two numbers of Bizkaitarra, June 1893 to September 1895
The Amorrortu press of Bilbao, whose descendants print the Obras Completas in Buenos Aires in 1965
sources: sabinoarana.eus, efeméride on Sebastián de Amorrortu

stops.name: Castejón, the banner sent to Navarre
stops.date_confidence: attested to 18 February 1894 by the pool's chronology and by eu.wikipedia. The quotation is dated two months after the journey, at 22 April 1894, and its wording follows Granja's own footnote against a garbled version carried in the pool, which had inverted the sense.
stops.campa: Navarre is refusing the finance minister's plan to tax it like any other province, and the refusal has become a general Basque cause that the country calls the Gamazada. Two months after the journey he prints the article that states it without cover: fuerismo, the defence of the old law, is separatism, and everyone who has ever defended the fueros has been a separatist without noticing. He goes south with Luis and a party of companions, carrying a banner that reads, in substance, God and Old Law, Biscay greets Navarre. It is the old Carlist watchword put to new work.
stops.quote: a que Bizkaya se constituya en nación perfectamente independiente sin otras relaciones con España que las internacionales.
stops.quote_source: 'Fuerismo es separatismo', Bizkaitarra, 22 April 1894, no. 8, in Obras Completas (1965), p. 267, as quoted by José Luis de la Granja Sainz
suggested_refs: The Gamazada of 1893-1894 and the Navarrese resistance to Germán Gamazo's fiscal project
'Fuerismo es separatismo', Bizkaitarra, 22 April 1894

stops.name: Bilbao, Euskeldun Batzokija and the flag on Calle Correo
stops.date_confidence: attested to 14 July 1894 by eu.wikipedia and es.wikipedia. Arana's election as president of the club's board, following a mass at the basilica of Begoña, is attested for the following day and is narrated in the same stop.
stops.campa: The first nationalist club opens at number 22 of Calle Correo, in the seven streets of the old town, and at six in the evening Ciriaco de Iturri, its oldest member and a former Carlist officer, runs up a flag: red field, green cross of Saint Andrew, white cross laid over it. The brothers had designed it for Biscay alone, and no province beyond Biscay is mentioned in the design. The following morning, after mass at the basilica of Begoña, the members elect Sabino president of the board. He is twenty-nine.
stops.quote: Your race, unique because of its beautiful qualities, but even more so because it does not have any contact points or fraternity with either the Spanish race or the French race, which are its neighbors, or with any race whatsoever in the world, is the one upon which your Bizkaya Fatherland was founded.
stops.quote_source: 'Nuestra voz', Bizkaitarra, 30 September 1894, in the English translation given by Politika.io, 'Basques, Jews, and the Racialization of Spanish Identity'
suggested_refs: Euskeldun Batzokija, Calle Correo 22, Bilbao, first nationalist club and first raising of the ikurriña
sources: politika.io, 'Basques, Jews, and the Racialization of Spanish Identity'

stops.name: Bilbao, the first Bizkai Buru Batzar
stops.date_confidence: attested to July 1895 by es.wikipedia. The day, 31 July, the feast of Ignatius of Loyola, and the list of the first executive come from the pool's chronology and were not independently confirmed.
stops.campa: On the feast of the Basque soldier who founded the Jesuits, in the club room on Calle Correo, seven men constitute an executive: Sabino as president, Luis, Fabián de Ispizua, Elías de Lekue, Juan de Aranburuzabala, Ciriaco de Llodio, Salvador de Etxeita. They call it the Bizkai Buru Batzar, the Biscay governing council. What is founded in the room is a party for one province, on the argument that autonomy is a fraud and only independence is a nation. The initials taken from that afternoon are still governing in Vitoria.
stops.quote: Aunque autonomía significa independencia, sin embargo sabido es que la autonomía que en estos tiempos tanto se cacarea, es la autonomía relativa y parcial, la autonomía regional; no la independencia absoluta y total, la independencia nacional.
stops.quote_source: 'La ceguera de los vizcaínos', Bizkaitarra, 30 September 1894, no. 15, in Obras Completas (1965), p. 371, as quoted by José Luis de la Granja Sainz
suggested_refs: The first Bizkai Buru Batzar of July 1895, organisational founding of EAJ-PNV

stops.name: Bilbao, the trial over a neighbour
stops.date_confidence: corrected: 10 August 1895 is the day he appeared at trial, not the day of conviction. es.wikipedia reads that on 10 August Sabino appears at the hearing; the sentence of one month and eleven days plus a fine follows, and imprisonment begins on 28 August. Courthouse coordinates are approximate.
stops.campa: The charge is not sedition. It is insulting a neighbour, the physician Filomeno Soltura, in the pages of Bizkaitarra, and a state has an easier time with libel than with doctrine. The paper that brought him here has spent two years sorting the province into natives and maketos, a word for the Spanish incomer that he did more than any man alive to sharpen. What the court fines him for is one paragraph about a doctor. He is offered a settlement beforehand and refuses to take it.
stops.quote: Today, when so many Bizkaino families are mixed with maketos, or Spaniards, thanks to Bizkainos who have already lost awareness of their nationality, we shall establish (if we are free to do so) a distinction between natives and mestizos, with regard to rights and to the places where they are permitted to settle; but someone of pure maketa race will ever be maketo, even if he is a descendant of seven generations born in Bizkaya, and a speaker of Euzkera.
stops.quote_source: 'Maketería y maketismo', Bizkaitarra, 2 February 1895, in the English translation given by Politika.io, 'Basques, Jews, and the Racialization of Spanish Identity'
suggested_refs: The Soltura libel prosecution of 1895 and its sentence of one month and eleven days
sources: politika.io, 'Basques, Jews, and the Racialization of Spanish Identity'

stops.name: Larrinaga, the gate at Solokoetxe
stops.date_confidence: attested: es.wikipedia gives 28 August 1895 for the entry into Larrinaga prison. Coordinates corrected to Larrinaga street in Solokoetxe, on the eastern hillside; the value first carried in the pool fell about a kilometre and a half away, across the ría in Deusto. The title of the quoted 1895 article was not specified by the citing source.
stops.campa: The sentence should run out on 8 October. It does not: other proceedings accumulate against him and against the club, and he stays in until January. On 12 September the authorities order Euskeldun Batzokija sealed and Bizkaitarra suppressed on a charge of inciting rebellion, and put its hundred and ten members through the courts. He goes on writing from the cell, and what he writes there is that nationality is settled by descent and not by birthplace. He will go on making that argument for the rest of his life.
stops.quote: to be born in one place or another does not mean anything, as is clearly the case with regards to race. A child of Bizkainos born in Madagascar or Dahomey will be as racially Bizkaino as anyone born in Olakueta; in turn, a descendant of Spaniards born in Bizkaya will never be racially Bizkaino.
stops.quote_source: Sabino Arana, article of 1895, title not specified by the citing source, in the English translation given by Politika.io, 'Basques, Jews, and the Racialization of Spanish Identity'
suggested_refs: The Cárcel de Larrinaga at Solokoetxe, Bilbao, demolished; site of both imprisonments
sources: politika.io, 'Basques, Jews, and the Racialization of Spanish Identity'

stops.name: Bilbao, out on reduced bail
stops.date_confidence: attested to January 1896 by es.wikipedia; the day, 13 January, comes from the pool's synthesis of the 1895-1896 prosecution cycle and was not independently confirmed. The absolution on the charge of inciting rebellion is attested by es.wikipedia for November 1896 and is narrated in the same stop.
stops.campa: The bail terms are reduced and he walks out after four and a half months into a province where his club is sealed and his paper is dead. He is thirty-one. In November a court absolves him of the rebellion charge altogether, so that the year's whole result is a state proving in public that his politics were legal and his manners were not. He begins again with new titles, new presses and the identical argument. The second time, the movement grows faster.
suggested_refs: The November 1896 absolution on the charge of incitement to rebellion

stops.name: Bilbao, elected provincial deputy
stops.date_confidence: attested verbatim by es.wikipedia to 11 September 1898; he holds the seat until 1902. Coordinates corrected to the OpenStreetMap geocode of the Bizkaiko Foru Aldundia on Arbieto kalea, about four hundred metres from the value first carried in the pool.
stops.campa: Spain loses Cuba, the Philippines and Puerto Rico in a single summer, and that autumn the man who calls the Spanish state a foreign power is elected to the provincial deputation of Biscay. He sits mostly alone. His interventions are about the Basque language, the administration of the province, and the protection of native Biscayans against incomers, and he tells other deputies to their faces that they bought their seats. In the same season a crowd gathers outside his house and stones it.
suggested_refs: The Diputación de Bizkaia, Arana's seat from September 1898 to 1902

stops.name: Abiña, the farmhouse in the estuary
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to date: es.wikipedia attests a courtship of one year before the marriage of 2 February 1900, which places the meeting in 1899, while the pool's geography lens gives only the 1890s. Month and day defaulted to 01. Coordinates corrected to the OpenStreetMap geocode of Abiña in Busturia, about three kilometres from the value first carried.
stops.campa: Nicolasa Achica-Allende was born at the Abiña baserri in 1873 to a poor rural family, in the Urdaibai estuary where he has been coming for years to breathe better air. He calls her Nikole. Before he will marry her he arranges her religious instruction with Carmelite nuns, and the letters he sends through the courtship instruct her in nearly everything else; they survive, and they are not gentle. Part of his family and part of his party think an aldeana beneath him. He marries her anyway.
suggested_refs: The Arana-Achica-Allende correspondence, reported on by DEIA in 2009 as 'Nikole maitia'
sources: research pool, geography lens (deia.eus article returned HTTP 406 and was not read)

stops.name: Bilbao, five councillors and the decree
stops.date_confidence: attested: es.wikipedia gives 14 May 1899 for the municipal elections that returned five nationalist councillors in Bilbao, and 15 May 1899 for the royal decree suspending constitutional guarantees in Biscay, which is narrated in the same stop. The restoration of guarantees is attested for April 1900.
stops.campa: On the Sunday the nationalists take five seats on the Bilbao council, the first time the doctrine converts into offices. On the Monday a royal decree suspends constitutional guarantees across Biscay, and the nationalist centres and papers, his among them, are closed. The sequence is not a coincidence and nobody troubles to disguise it as one. In the eleven months that follow, the movement learns how fast it grows under prohibition. Guarantees are restored in April 1900, the centres reopen, and he is still a sitting deputy of the province that has just been suspended.
suggested_refs: The royal decree of 15 May 1899 suspending constitutional guarantees in Biscay

stops.name: Bilbao, El Correo Vasco
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the day: es.wikipedia gives June 1899 for the launch of El Correo Vasco, and the pool's chronology adds 4 June and a closure on 15 September after 103 numbers. The office address was not located and the pin marks the old-town publishing district.
stops.campa: A daily this time, not a broadsheet. He and Luis put their own money into it, work the nights, correct the proofs, and run it for a hundred and three numbers before it folds in September. The paper is born under a suspension of constitutional guarantees and dies of its own accounts. The brothers are good at founding things and poor at financing them. In August, on its front pages, he prints the most explicit statement of the doctrine of isolation he ever set down, and what the doctrine asks for is removal.
stops.quote: the salvation of Basque society, its regeneration and its future hope, depend on the most absolute isolation, on the removal of every foreign element, on the rational and practical exclusion of everything that does not clearly bear the fixed and indelible imprint of pure Basque origins.
stops.quote_source: 'Extranjerización', El Correo Vasco, 10 August 1899, in the English translation given by Politika.io, 'Basques, Jews, and the Racialization of Spanish Identity'
suggested_refs: El Correo Vasco, Bilbao, June to September 1899, 103 numbers
sources: politika.io, 'Basques, Jews, and the Racialization of Spanish Identity'

stops.name: Abiña, the wedding in the hermitage
stops.date_confidence: attested to 2 February 1900 by es.wikipedia and en.wikipedia, after a courtship of one year. Coordinates corrected to the OpenStreetMap geocode of the hermitage at Axpe, Busturia; the place name should read Busturia rather than Pedernales.
stops.campa: They marry quietly in the hermitage above the farmstead, partly to keep off the crowd that would come to watch the founder of Basque nationalism marry a farm girl. Through the marriage the islet of San Andrés, which belongs to the Abiña baserri, passes into his hands. It is the last event of his life he manages to keep private. He is thirty-five and has three years and ten months left; Nikole is twenty-seven, and the letters he wrote her through the courtship will wait a hundred and nine years to be reported on.
suggested_refs: The hermitage of San Antonio de Abiña, Busturia
The islet of San Andrés, held through the marriage and sold by his widow in 1906

stops.name: Lourdes, the honeymoon at the grotto
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the Lourdes honeymoon appears in the pool's family-biography synthesis and in none of the Spanish, English or Basque Wikipedia articles, and could not be independently confirmed. Only the year 1900 is given by the source; the date is placed immediately after the attested wedding of 2 February for ordering. Coordinates corrected to the sanctuary itself rather than the town centre.
stops.campa: The grotto where a miller's daughter saw the Virgin forty-two years earlier is by now the largest pilgrimage machine in Europe, and it is a few hours from Bilbao on the French side of the mountains. The most devoutly Catholic politician in Spain takes his new wife there. It is the only crossing into France in his adult life that is not flight, exile or a philological congress, and it is also the worst attested: nothing in the record says what he did at the baths or in the basilica, and no letter from the trip has come to light.
suggested_refs: The Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes
sources: research pool, geography lens (dossier synthesis of family biography; unconfirmed)

stops.name: Sukarrieta, the child that does not arrive
stops.date_confidence: attested: es.wikipedia records that in August 1900 Nikole, four months pregnant, lost the child they were expecting. The day is not given and is defaulted to 01. Coordinates corrected: the pool carried three different values for Sukarrieta across its lenses, and the one used follows the coordinates given in es.wikipedia's own article on the municipality, which OpenStreetMap corroborates.
stops.campa: Four months in, in the rented house at Sukarrieta, Nikole loses the child they were expecting. He is thirty-five, he is building a doctrine in which what makes a Biscayan is eight surnames and not a birthplace, and he will leave no descendant to carry any of the eight. What inherits him is the party: Luis, then Ángel de Zabala, then a hundred and twenty years of men who never met him. Of the pregnancy itself the record keeps one line, August 1900, four months, the child lost. No other is documented for the marriage.
suggested_refs: The rented house at Sukarrieta, home of the marriage from 1900

stops.name: Hendaye, the congress on spelling
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1901 by es.wikipedia, which says only that during that year Arana took part as vice-president in the orthographic congress at Hendaye; the day of 16 September carried in the pool is unsupported and the date is defaulted to 01. eu.wikipedia independently confirms the 1901 founding at Hendaye and lists Arana, Azkue, Campión and Adema among some thirty-five founders, without assigning offices, so the joint vice-presidency with Campión remains attributed rather than documented.
stops.campa: Back over the Bidasoa, into the town his family crossed into as refugees twenty-eight years before, he sits as joint vice-president with Arturo Campión at a congress convened to settle how Basque should be written. Azkue is in the room, holding the chair Arana failed to win in 1888. Arana wants a unified orthography and refuses a unified language: one supradialectal standard, he argues, would erase the provincial varieties it claims to serve. The quarrel is over substance and not procedure, and the question of a standard Basque is still open when he dies two years later.
suggested_refs: The Hendaye orthographic congress of 1901 and the founding of Euskaltzaleen Biltzarra

segments.name: The Telegram and the Second Prison

stops.name: Bilbao, the Centro Vasco sacked
stops.date_confidence: attested to May 1902 by es.wikipedia; the day is not given and is defaulted to 01. The Centro Vasco had been founded around 1899 as a nominally apolitical social venue; its exact address was not located and the pin marks the old town at city-block precision.
stops.campa: The nominally apolitical Basque Centre, opened so that the movement would have a room that was not a party office, is broken into and wrecked by opponents. It is the ordinary weather of Bilbao politics by now: a royal decree in one year, a crowd stoning his house in another, a sacking in a third, and prosecutions running underneath the whole time. He is thirty-seven, in the last months of his seat on the deputation, and the province he wants to detach from Spain is more Spanish every year as the ore trade pulls in labour. Three weeks later he walks into the post office.
suggested_refs: The Centro Vasco of Bilbao, founded 1899, sacked May 1902

stops.name: Bilbao, the telegram to Roosevelt
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the day: the Sabino Arana Fundazioa gives 24 May 1902 and the Wikisource transcription is headed 24 or 25 May, while es.wikipedia dates the episode to May 1902 without a day. A variant wording of the same telegram circulates, differing in word order and punctuation, which points to transcription variance rather than two separate messages. The pin approximates the historic Bilbao post office at city-block precision.
stops.campa: He writes it in the name of the Basque Nationalist Party and hands it across the counter: congratulations to the President of the United States on the independence of Cuba, praise for a federation that freed what it had held, and then one clause too many. If Europe imitated the example, the Basque nation would be free as well. The message never leaves Bilbao. It goes to the authorities instead, who read that clause exactly as he wrote it, and the charge is rebellion against the integrity of the Spanish nation.
stops.quote: Roosevelt, Presidente Estados Unidos. Washington. Nombre Partido Nacionalista Vasco felicito por independencia Cuba por Federación nobilísima que presidís, que supo liberar la esclavitud. Ejemplo magnanimidad y culto justicia y libertad dan vuestros poderosos estados, desconocido Historia, e inimitable para potencias Europa, particularmente latinas. Si Europa imitara, también nación vasca, su pueblo más antiguo, que más siglos gozó libertad rigiéndose Constitución que mereció elogios Estados Unidos, sería libre. Arana Goiri.
stops.quote_source: Telegram, Sabino Arana to Theodore Roosevelt, 24 or 25 May 1902, as reproduced at es.wikisource.org, 'Telegrama de Sabino Arana a Theodore Roosevelt'
suggested_refs: The intercepted Roosevelt telegram of May 1902, es.wikisource transcription
The Sabino Arana Fundazioa efeméride on the telegram, giving a variant wording
sources: es.wikisource.org, 'Telegrama de Sabino Arana a Theodore Roosevelt'

stops.name: Larrinaga, arrested for a message that never arrived
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the date of 30 May 1902, the judge Mauro Santiago Portero, the amended article 248 of the Penal Code, the prosecutor's demand of eight years and one day and the reported nine thousand signatures all come from the Sabino Arana Fundazioa's account and were not independently confirmed. Coordinates corrected to Larrinaga in Solokoetxe.
stops.campa: Back through the same gate, seven years after the first time. The prosecutor asks for eight years and one day under an article about the integrity of the nation, and the judge is Mauro Santiago Portero. The story that prison killed him begins in this cell; it is a story rather than a diagnosis, and it will be repeated for a century. He is already ill in ways nobody has yet named. More than nine thousand people are said to sign for his release on grounds of health, and the courts refuse them.
suggested_refs: Article 248 of the Spanish Penal Code as amended, under which the rebellion charge was framed
sources: sabinoarana.eus, efeméride on the Roosevelt telegram episode

stops.name: Larrinaga, the article from the cell
stops.date_confidence: attested: es.wikipedia records that on 22 June 1902, from prison, Arana published an article called Grave y transcendental, spelling it so. The venue La Patria and the label Liga de Vascos Españolistas come from the pool's synthesis and appear in none of the fetched sources. Granja does not name the document the quoted phrase comes from, citing only Corcuera for it.
stops.campa: Twenty-three days into the second imprisonment he publishes an article proposing to wind up the openly separatist party and put in its place a legal organisation seeking the most radical autonomy possible within the unity of the Spanish state. The man who wrote in 1888 that autonomy would be Euskeria's death sentence is now proposing autonomy. Whether this was tactics, exhaustion, illness or a change of mind has been argued for a hundred and twenty years. He died before anyone could make him say.
stops.quote: una autonomía lo más radical posible dentro de la unidad del estado español
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Arana on the projected programme of the Liga de Vascos Españolistas, 1902, quoted with that attribution in José Luis de la Granja Sainz, 'La concepción de la autonomía en el pensamiento político del Nacionalismo Vasco: I. La Restauración', citing J. Corcuera, Orígenes, ideología y organización del nacionalismo vasco (1979)
suggested_refs: 'Grave y transcendental', 22 June 1902
Santiago de Pablo and José Luis de la Granja, 2009, on the Arana-Eleizalde correspondence

stops.name: Bilbao, acquitted, and gone by evening
stops.date_confidence: attested to 8 November 1902 by es.wikipedia: the jury acquits and the prosecutor at once announces an appeal. Courthouse coordinates are approximate and the footprint of the historic Audiencia was not verified. The crossing into France under the name Sylvain de Arbeste is attested for 1902 without a date and is narrated in the same stop; the crossing point is not specified by any source and Hendaye is the conventional one.
stops.campa: A jury acquits him. The prosecutor stands and announces an appeal, which leaves the eight years and one day still on the table, and so he crosses the border and waits on the French side, signing himself Sylvain de Arbeste: a French name for a Biscayan hiding from a Spanish court. It is the fourth time the Bidasoa has served his family as an exit, and the first since the Carlist flight of 1873. Not convicted and not exiled, a free man travelling under a name that is not his, he is thirty-seven years old and has twelve months to live.
suggested_refs: The November 1902 jury acquittal at the Audiencia de Bilbao and the prosecutor's appeal

stops.name: Sukarrieta, the play called Libe
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: March 1903 for Libe, a four-act historical musical drama on the fifteenth-century battle of Mungia published under the pseudonym Jelalde, comes from the pool's chronology and was not independently refetched. The day is defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: In the rented house at the top of the Arrospe slope he writes a play: four acts, music, a fifteenth-century battle at Mungia, and a heroine called Libe who is offered to the audience as a type to be copied. He had begun writing at nineteen with an essay on Basque orthography, and he finishes with a chorus and a costume. It is the last substantial thing he sets down, a patriotic theatre for a nation that does not exist yet, and he is writing it in a house he does not own and can no longer walk far from. He signs it Jelalde, which fools nobody.
suggested_refs: Libe, four-act drama on the battle of Mungia, published under the pseudonym Jelalde, 1903
sources: research pool, chronology lens (dossier crawl, not independently refetched)

stops.name: Sukarrieta, a name for the illness
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: August 1903 for the diagnosis of Addison's disease, and the physician Carlos de Iruarrizaga, come from the pool's dossier synthesis and were not independently refetched. The day is defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: The doctor gives it a name. Addison's disease, failure of the adrenal glands, described by Thomas Addison half a century earlier and untreatable in 1903. The lungs at sixteen, the stomach through the middle years, and now this. He is thirty-eight. In late October the symptoms turn sharply worse and the household begins to arrange itself around a dying man. The movement will say afterwards that Larrinaga did this to him, that the cell and the bad air killed him, and the adrenal glands do not fail that way. Reference works still repeat it.
suggested_refs: Carlos de Iruarrizaga, the physician who gave the diagnosis
sources: research pool, chronology and geography lenses (dossier synthesis, not independently refetched)

stops.name: Sukarrieta, the movement handed to Kondaño
stops.date_confidence: attested to September 1903 by es.wikipedia, which records that Arana leaves the direction of the PNV because of the advanced state of his illness and names Ángel de Zabala as successor. The exact day of 30 September carried in the pool is unsupported and the day is defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He chooses Ángel Zabala Ozámiz, called Kondaño, and hands the movement over. Zabala is an unambiguous independentist, which settles in practice the question the article from the cell had opened fifteen months earlier: whatever Arana meant by the most radical autonomy possible, he does not leave the party to a man who would go looking for it. The succession is his last political act, and he performs it in a house he does not own, at the far end of an estuary, without going back to Bilbao.
suggested_refs: Ángel de Zabala Ozámiz, 'Kondaño', president of the PNV from 1903

stops.name: Sukarrieta, the death at thirty-eight
stops.date_confidence: attested to 25 November 1903 at Pedernales, aged thirty-eight, by es.wikipedia and en.wikipedia. The causal claim that imprisonment produced the fatal Addison's disease is repeated by both articles and is not medically demonstrated; it is recorded here as contested rather than settled.
stops.campa: He dies in the rented house, in the municipality then called Pedernales, thirty-eight years old. The family who were with him report a long confession and observances complete to the last of them. Eleven years of public life had produced two newspapers, a club, a party, a flag, an orthography, a vocabulary, a calendar of invented given names, and a doctrine of blood the movement will spend the next century quarrelling about. The house was rented, the islet had come from his wife's family, and the party had been Zabala's since September.
suggested_refs: The rented house at the top of the Arrospe slope, Sukarrieta, since demolished

stops.name: Sukarrieta, the modest grave
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 1903; the day is not given by any source and is placed the day after the death for ordering. Cemetery coordinates are approximate and the plot was not verified; they also sit some three kilometres from the corrected coordinates used elsewhere for Sukarrieta, and that discrepancy is recorded rather than resolved.
stops.campa: They bury him in the local cemetery. Disciples will propose a monumental mausoleum on the islet in the estuary, a place of pilgrimage they compare aloud to Rome and to Mecca, and after that an obelisk in the Egyptian manner. Neither gets built. The grave stays a grave, and no source reached describes a headstone, a restoration or an annual rite there. Within three years his widow sells the islet to Claudio Urrutia for fifteen thousand pesetas, partly to keep an explosives company from buying it.
suggested_refs: The cemetery of Sukarrieta, formerly Pedernales
The islet of San Andrés, sold by Nicolasa Achica-Allende in 1906

stops.name: Sukarrieta, the house erased from the hill
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The sale of the islet of San Andrés by Arana's widow in 1906 is attested by es.wikipedia's article on Sukarrieta and fixes the year used here to order the segment. The later passage of the Sukarrieta property to the shipping magnate Ramón de la Sota, its use as a chalet, and its eventual conversion into maritime colonies after the death of Sota's daughter come from naiz.eus and were not independently confirmed.
stops.campa: The rented house at the top of the slope does not become a shrine. It passes into the hands of the shipping fortune of Ramón de la Sota, serves as a chalet, and after the death of Sota's daughter is turned over to maritime colonies. Buildings come down and paths close, and no source reached names the room he died in or says whether it was standing when the chalet went up. The movement builds its memory somewhere else. Onto the ground where the founder of Basque nationalism died, working-class children out of Bilbao are sent for their lungs.
suggested_refs: The colonias marítimas of Sukarrieta, on the site associated with Arana's last house

stops.name: Bilbao, the flag becomes the flag
stops.date_confidence: attested: es.wikipedia's article on the ikurriña gives 19 October 1936 for its adoption by the provisional presidency of the Basque Government, 19 January 1977 for its legalisation in Spain, and article 5 of the Statute of Autonomy of 25 October 1979 for its establishment as the official flag. That source dates the prohibition to the aftermath of the 1936 coup; the 1938 start date carried in the pool from nabasque.eus is not corroborated. The stop sits at the pin where the flag was first raised in 1894, not at any later site.
stops.campa: Forty-two years after Ciriaco de Iturri ran it up outside the club on Calle Correo, the cloth the two brothers cut for one province is declared the flag of a government. It is banned within months and stays banned for four decades, legal only on the French side, drawn on walls and folded into drawers. It is legalised again in January 1977 and written into the Statute of Autonomy in 1979, as the flag of three provinces it was never designed for. Nobody has proposed changing it since.
suggested_refs: The ikurriña, designed 1894, official flag of the Basque Country under article 5 of the 1979 Statute of Autonomy

stops.name: Abando, Sabin Etxea razed and rebuilt
stops.date_confidence: attested by es.wikipedia's article on Sabin Etxea: the house built in 1857 by Santiago Arana, seized by the Falange in 1937 after the fall of Bilbao, used for years by Auxilio Social, its demolition decided in December 1960 and carried out between 1960 and 1961; the lot bought back by the PNV in 1979, a competition won in 1988 by Koldo Eguren Zendoia, the new building of 7,993 square metres occupied from October 1992 and finished in 1995. The 1937 date opens the span. That source calls the original a neo-Basque palacete rather than a neoclassical one. The first Aberri Eguna of 27 March 1932, narrated in the same stop, is dated by sabinoarana.eus.
stops.campa: On 27 March 1932, fifty years after the conversation in the garden, the first Aberri Eguna ends at the restored birth house and a plaque goes up on the wall marking the spot. Five years later the Falange takes the building and Franco's welfare organisation works out of it; in the winter of 1960 the authorities decide to pull it down, and by 1961 the lot is bare. The party buys the empty address back in 1979 and raises a new headquarters on it, occupied in 1992. Nothing of the 1857 house survives inside it.
suggested_refs: Sabin Etxea, Ibáñez de Bilbao 16, headquarters of EAJ-PNV since 1992
The first Aberri Eguna, Bilbao, 27 March 1932
sources: sabinoarana.eus, page on the first Aberri Eguna

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Obras Completas
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the account of Sabindiar Batza, founded at Bayonne on 14 September 1950 by some thirty PNV members, and the printing of the Obras Completas by Artes Gráficas Amorrortu in Buenos Aires on 17 April 1965 in 2,450 leather-bound copies of 2,478 pages, distributed roughly 1,700 to Bayonne and 500 to Venezuela, comes from the Sabino Arana Fundazioa and was not independently confirmed. Arana never travelled to Buenos Aires; this stop belongs to his scattered writings, not to his body. The pin is the canonical Buenos Aires coordinate.
stops.campa: The exile institute founded at Bayonne in 1950 spends fifteen years gathering everything he ever printed, article by article, out of dead newspapers, and has it set in Buenos Aires by the descendants of Sebastián de Amorrortu, who printed Bizkaitarra on a Bilbao hand press seventy years before. Two thousand four hundred and fifty copies, leather-bound, nearly twenty-five hundred pages, published on Aberri Eguna in the centenary year of his birth. Seventeen hundred go to Bayonne, five hundred to Venezuela, the rest across the Americas to men who will never see Biscay again.
suggested_refs: Obras Completas, Sabindiar-Batza, Bayonne and Buenos Aires, 17 April 1965
Artes Gráficas Amorrortu, Buenos Aires, successors of the Bilbao press that printed Bizkaitarra
sources: sabinoarana.eus, 'Sabindiar Batza y la recopilación de las Obras Completas de Sabino de Arana y Goiri' (14 September 2023)

stops.name: Bilbao, the statue in the Jardines de Albia
stops.date_confidence: the statue in the Jardines de Albia, in the part of the garden nearest the Palace of Justice, is attested by es.wikipedia's article on the gardens, which gives neither sculptor nor installation date; both remain gaps that no source reached could fill. Coordinates corrected to the OpenStreetMap artwork node. The date is February 2017, when the People's Party of the Basque Country called for renaming streets named after him, attested by en.wikipedia; day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He stands in bronze in a small garden two streets from where he was born, close to the courthouse, and nobody reached can say who cast him or when. In February 2017 the People's Party of the Basque Country asks that the streets carrying his name be renamed, on the argument that he made ETA possible. An avenue, a metro entrance and a tram stop a kilometre west still carry it. Open Library lists twelve editions of his writing, every one of them in Spanish or Basque. The flag travelled and the word abertzale travelled; the writing stayed home.
suggested_refs: The Sabino Arana statue, Jardines de Albia, Bilbao, sculptor and date unrecorded in reachable sources
Open Library author record OL83579A, twelve editions, none in translation
